name: Chapter 4: Determinants
description: Determinants of order 2 and 3, area of a triangle, minors and cofactors, adjoint and inverse, solving linear systems, plus determinant properties and exam-style problems.

cards.term: What is the determinant of a square matrix?
cards.definition: A single number attached to a square matrix A, written det A or |A|. It exists only for square matrices; |A| is a number, A is an array

cards.term: Determinant of a 1 × 1 and a 2 × 2 matrix?
cards.definition: |[a]| = a. For A =\[\begin{bmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{bmatrix}\]: |A| = ad − bc (main diagonal minus the other diagonal)

cards.term: Example 1: evaluate |2 4; −1 2|. Ex 4.1 Q1: |2 4; −5 −1|.
cards.definition: 2·2 − 4(−1) = 8. For Ex 4.1 Q1: 2(−1) − 4(−5) = −2 + 20 = 18

cards.term: Ex 4.1 Q2: evaluate (i) |cos θ −sin θ; sin θ cos θ| and (ii) |x² − x + 1, x − 1; x + 1, x + 1|.
cards.definition: (i) cos²θ + sin²θ = 1. (ii) (x² − x + 1)(x + 1) − (x − 1)(x + 1) = (x³ + 1) − (x² − 1) = x³ − x² + 2

cards.term: Determinant is the area scale factor
cards.definition: |det A| is the factor by which A scales areas (volumes in 3D); det A = 0 collapses the plane onto a line; sign of det gives orientation; unit square -> parallelogram of area |ad-bc|

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Determinant as area

A = [[3, 1], [1, 2]] sends the unit square to a parallelogram. What is its area, and how does it relate to |A|?

Follow where the two unit vectors go.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Determinant as area

A = [[3, 1], [1, 2]] sends the unit square to a parallelogram. What is its area, and how does it relate to |A|?

The columns of A are the images of e₁ = (1, 0) and e₂ = (0, 1): (3, 1) and (1, 2). The unit square becomes the parallelogram they span, with area |ad − bc| = |3·2 − 1·1| = 5 = |A|.

So |det A| is the factor by which A scales areas. If det A < 0 the picture is also flipped (orientation reverses); if det A = 0 the square is squashed onto a line (no inverse).

cards.term: How do you expand a 3 × 3 determinant along the first row?
cards.definition: |A| = a₁₁ |a₂₂ a₂₃; a₃₂ a₃₃| − a₁₂ |a₂₁ a₂₃; a₃₁ a₃₃| + a₁₃ |a₂₁ a₂₂; a₃₁ a₃₂|. Signs alternate + − +. You can expand along any row or column with the sign pattern (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ

cards.term: Which row or column should you expand along?
cards.definition: The one with the most zeros (each zero kills a whole 2 × 2 term). Ex 4.1 Q5(i): expand along the second row [0 0 −1]: only one term survives

cards.term: Ex 4.1 Q3: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]Show |2A| = 4|A|.
cards.definition: |A| = 2 − 8 = −6. 2A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 8 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]has determinant 8 − 32 = −24 = 4(−6). ✓ In general |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix

cards.term: Ex 4.1 Q4: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]Show |3A| = 27|A|.
cards.definition: A is upper triangular: |A| = 1·1·4 = 4. 3A has diagonal 3, 3, 12, so |3A| = 108 = 27 · 4. ✓ (3³ = 27 because n = 3)

cards.term: Determinant of a triangular or diagonal matrix?
cards.definition: The product of the diagonal entries (all zeros on one side of the diagonal). So |I| = 1
Expand along row 1: 3(0 − 5) + 1(0 + 3) − 2(0 − 0) = −15 + 3 = −12. (Row 2 has two zeros, so expanding along it is quicker: only −1 survives.)
0 − 1(0 − 6) + 2(−3 − 0) = 6 − 6 = 0. The matrix is skew-symmetric of odd order (a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order always has determinant 0)

cards.term: Ex 4.1 Q6: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 5 & 4 & -9\end{bmatrix}\]Find |A|.
cards.definition: 1(−9 + 12) − 1(−18 + 15) − 2(8 − 5) = 3 + 3 − 6 = 0 (so A is singular)

cards.term: Example 5 / Ex 4.1 Q7(i): find x if |2 4; 5 1| = |2x 4; 6 x|.
cards.definition: 2 − 20 = 2x² − 24 → 2x² = 6 → x = ±√3
10 − 12 = −2 = 5x − 6x = −x → x = 2
x² − 36 = 36 − 36 = 0 → x² = 36 → (B) ±6

cards.term: Example 5: find x for which |3 x; x 1| = |3 2; 4 1|.
cards.definition: 3 − x² = 3 − 8 → x² = 8 → x = ±2√2

cards.term: Area of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃) as a determinant?
cards.definition: Δ = ½ |x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1|. Take the absolute value; the determinant itself can be negative

cards.term: Area of a triangle from vertices by determinant
cards.definition: Area = 1/2 |det [x1 y1 1; x2 y2 1; x3 y3 1]|, absolute value; use +- when area is given; zero for collinear points; (3,8),(-4,2),(5,1) gives 61/2

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Area of a triangle

Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3, 8), (−4, 2) and (5, 1) using a determinant.

Put the coordinates in the determinant with a column of 1s.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Area of a triangle

Find the area of the triangle with vertices (3, 8), (−4, 2) and (5, 1) using a determinant.

Δ = ½ |x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1|. Expanding: ½ [3(2 − 1) − 8(−4 − 5) + 1(−4 − 10)] = ½ (3 + 72 − 14) = 61/2 square units.

Take the absolute value for an area. If the area is given, use both ±. If the three points are collinear the determinant is 0.

cards.term: If the area is given, how do you use the determinant?
cards.definition: Set ½ |...| = ±(area), i.e. use both signs, and solve for the unknown (Example 7: two values of k)

cards.term: Collinearity test with a determinant
cards.definition: Three points are collinear iff |x1 y1 1; x2 y2 1; x3 y3 1| = 0; A(a,b+c), B(b,c+a), C(c,a+b) all lie on x+y=a+b+c

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Collinear points

Show that A(a, b + c), B(b, c + a), C(c, a + b) are collinear.

What do x + y equal at each point?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Collinear points

Show that A(a, b + c), B(b, c + a), C(c, a + b) are collinear.

The area determinant is ½ |a b+c 1; b c+a 1; c a+b 1|. Add column 1 to column 2: the second column becomes (a+b+c, a+b+c, a+b+c), a multiple of the third column, so the determinant is 0.

Geometrically all three points satisfy x + y = a + b + c: they lie on one line. Three points are collinear ⇔ the area determinant is 0.

cards.term: Condition for three points to be collinear?
cards.definition: |x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1| = 0 (area zero). The same trick gives the equation of a line through two points: put P(x, y) as the third vertex

cards.term: Example 7: find the equation of the line through A(1, 3) and B(0, 0) using determinants; find k if D(k, 0) makes area ABD = 3.
cards.definition: |0 0 1; 1 3 1; x y 1| = 0 → y − 3x = 0: y = 3x. Area: ½ |1 3 1; 0 0 1; k 0 1| = ½ |−3k| = 3 → k = ±2
½ [−2(2 + 8) + 3(−8 + 3) − 1(−3 − 2)] = ½ (−20 − 15 + 5) = ½ (−30). Area is the absolute value: 15

cards.term: Ex 4.2 Q2: show A(a, b + c), B(b, c + a), C(c, a + b) are collinear.
cards.definition: Add column 1 to column 2: column 2 becomes (a + b + c) in every row, a multiple of column 3 (all 1s). Two proportional columns ⇒ determinant 0. Collinear

cards.term: Ex 4.2 Q3(i): find k if the triangle (k, 0), (4, 0), (0, 2) has area 4.
cards.definition: Area = ½ · |k − 4| · 2 = |k − 4| = 4 → k = 0 or 8

cards.term: Ex 4.2 Q3(ii): find k if the triangle (−2, 0), (0, 4), (0, k) has area 4.
cards.definition: Base on the y-axis |4 − k|, height 2: ½ · 2 · |4 − k| = 4 → k = 0 or 8

cards.term:
Ex 4.2 Q4: equation of the line through
(i) (1, 2) and (3, 6)
(ii) (3, 1) and (9, 3), using determinants.

Ex 4.2 Q5: area 35 sq units with vertices (2, −6), (5, 4), (k, 4). Then k =
(A) 12
(B) −2
(C) −12, −2
(D) 12, −2
cards.definition: Base (5, 4) to (k, 4) has length |k − 5|, height 10: ½ · 10 · |k − 5| = 35 → |k − 5| = 7 → (D) 12, −2

cards.term: Define the minor of an element aᵢⱼ.
cards.definition: Mᵢⱼ = the determinant left after deleting the i-th row and j-th column

cards.term: Define the cofactor of aᵢⱼ.
cards.definition: Aᵢⱼ = (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ Mᵢⱼ. Sign pattern for 3 × 3: + − + / − + − / + − +

cards.term: Minor and cofactor: delete row and column, then sign
cards.definition: Minor M_ij = determinant after deleting row i and column j; cofactor A_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij; |A| = sum a_ij A_ij along any row or column; a row times another row cofactors = 0

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Minors and cofactors

For a 3 × 3 determinant, how do you find the minor and the cofactor of a₁₂?

Delete the row and column of a₁₂.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Minors and cofactors

For a 3 × 3 determinant, how do you find the minor and the cofactor of a₁₂?

Minor Mᵢⱼ: cross out row i and column j, and take the determinant of what remains (here a 2 × 2).

Cofactor Aᵢⱼ = (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ Mᵢⱼ: attach the checkerboard sign (+ at a₁₁, − at a₁₂, …). Then |A| = Σⱼ aᵢⱼ Aᵢⱼ along any row or column; but multiplying a row by the cofactors of another row gives 0.

cards.term: Expansion by cofactors: what is |A| in terms of aᵢⱼ and Aᵢⱼ? What if the cofactors belong to another row?
cards.definition: |A| = Σⱼ aᵢⱼ Aᵢⱼ (any fixed row i or column j). But Σⱼ aᵢⱼ Aₖⱼ = 0 for k ≠ i: a row times the cofactors of another row is 0

cards.term:
Ex 4.3 Q5: if Δ = |aᵢⱼ| and Aᵢⱼ is the cofactor of aᵢⱼ, then Δ =
(A) a₁₁A₃₁ + a₁₂A₃₂ + a₁₃A₃₃
(B) a₁₁A₁₁ + a₁₂A₂₁ + a₁₃A₃₁
(C) a₂₁A₁₁ + a₂₂A₁₂ + a₂₃A₁₃
(D) a₁₁A₁₁ + a₂₁A₂₁ + a₃₁A₃₁
cards.definition: Row or column of elements with the SAME row/column of cofactors: (D) is the first column with its own cofactors. (D)

cards.term: Ex 4.3 Q1(i): minors and cofactors of |2 −4; 0 3|.
cards.definition: M₁₁ = 3, M₁₂ = 0, M₂₁ = −4, M₂₂ = 2. Cofactors: A₁₁ = 3, A₁₂ = 0, A₂₁ = 4, A₂₂ = 2

cards.term: Ex 4.3 Q1(ii): minors and cofactors of |a c; b d|.
cards.definition: M₁₁ = d, M₁₂ = b, M₂₁ = c, M₂₂ = a. Cofactors: A₁₁ = d, A₁₂ = −b, A₂₁ = −c, A₂₂ = a

cards.term: Ex 4.3 Q2(i): minors and cofactors of the 3 × 3 identity.
cards.definition: M₁₁ = M₂₂ = M₃₃ = 1 and all other minors 0; cofactors: A₁₁ = A₂₂ = A₃₃ = 1, others 0 (so the cofactor matrix is I)

cards.term: Ex 4.3 Q2(ii): cofactors of |1 0 4; 3 5 −1; 0 1 2|.
cards.definition: A₁₁ = 11, A₁₂ = −6, A₁₃ = 3; A₂₁ = 4, A₂₂ = 2, A₂₃ = −1; A₃₁ = −20, A₃₂ = 13, A₃₃ = 5. Check: |A| = 1·11 + 0 + 4·3 = 23

cards.term: Ex 4.3 Q3: using cofactors of the second row, evaluate |5 3 8; 2 0 1; 1 2 3|.
Ex 4.3 Q4: using cofactors of the third column, evaluate |1 x yz; 1 y zx; 1 z xy|.
Define the adjoint of a square matrix.
cards.definition: adj A = transpose of the cofactor matrix [Aᵢⱼ]. So (adj A)ᵢⱼ = Aⱼᵢ (note the swap)

cards.term: Shortcut for adj A when A is 2 × 2?
cards.definition: For A =\[\begin{bmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{bmatrix}\]: adj A =\[\begin{bmatrix}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{bmatrix}\](swap the diagonal, negate the others). Example 12: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]gives\[\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Theorem 1: A (adj A) = ?
cards.definition: (adj A) A = A (adj A) = |A| I. Reason: a row times its own cofactors gives |A|, times another row’s cofactors gives 0

cards.term: Define singular and non-singular matrices.
cards.definition: Singular: |A| = 0 (e.g.\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 8\end{bmatrix}\]). Non-singular: |A| ≠ 0

cards.term: Theorem 4: when is a square matrix invertible? Formula?
cards.definition: Iff it is non-singular (|A| ≠ 0), and then A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A

cards.term: Determinant of a product: |AB| = ?
cards.definition: |AB| = |A||B| (Theorem 3). So AB is non-singular iff both A and B are

cards.term: |adj A| for an n × n matrix?
cards.definition: |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹. For n = 3: |A|². For n = 2: |A|. (Ex 4.4 Q17: answer (B) |A|²)

cards.term: If A is invertible, |A⁻¹| = ?
cards.definition: 1/|A| since |A||A⁻¹| = |I| = 1 (Ex 4.4 Q18: (B))

cards.term:
Ex 4.4 Q17: A is a non-singular 3 × 3 matrix; |adj A| =
(A) |A|
(B) |A|²
(C) |A|³
(D) 3|A|
cards.definition: (B) |A|² (from |adj A||A| = |A|³)

cards.term:
Ex 4.4 Q18: A invertible of order 2; det(A⁻¹) =
(A) det A
(B) 1/det A
(C) 1
(D) 0
cards.definition: (B) 1/det A

cards.term: Method: find A⁻¹ using the adjoint (3 × 3).
cards.definition: 1) |A| ≠ 0? 2) all nine cofactors Aᵢⱼ. 3) adj A = transpose of the cofactor matrix. 4) A⁻¹ = adj A / |A|. Verify with A A⁻¹ = I

cards.term: Inverse by the adjoint method
cards.definition: A^-1 = adj A / |A|: compute |A|, cofactors, transpose, divide; Example 13: |A| = 1, A^-1 = [[7,-3,-3],[-1,1,0],[-1,0,1]]

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Adjoint method · Example 13

Find A⁻¹ for A = [[1, 3, 3], [1, 4, 3], [1, 3, 4]].

A = [[1, 3, 3], [1, 4, 3], [1, 3, 4]]
  1. |A| = 1(16 − 9) − 3(4 − 3) + 3(3 − 4) = 7 − 3 − 3 = 1 ≠ 0
  2. Cofactors: A₁₁ = 7, A₁₂ = −1, A₁₃ = −1, A₂₁ = −3, A₂₂ = 1, A₂₃ = 0, A₃₁ = −3, A₃₂ = 0, A₃₃ = 1
  3. adj A = transpose = [[7, −3, −3], [−1, 1, 0], [−1, 0, 1]]
  4. ?

cards.term: Example 15: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]Show A² − 4A + I = O and find A⁻¹.
cards.definition: A² =\[\begin{bmatrix}7 & 12 \\ 4 & 7\end{bmatrix}\]A² − 4A + I = O. Multiply by A⁻¹: A − 4I + A⁻¹ = O so A⁻¹ = 4I − A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q1: adj of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: Swap the diagonal, negate the rest:\[\begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q2: adj of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: Cofactor matrix then transpose:\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -11 \\ -12 & 5 & -1 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q3: verify A(adj A) = |A| I for A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ -4 & -6\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: adj A =\[\begin{bmatrix}-6 & -3 \\ 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]A(adj A) =\[\begin{bmatrix}-12 + 12 & -6 + 6 \\ 24 - 24 & 12 - 12\end{bmatrix}\]= O and |A| = −12 + 12 = 0, so |A|I = O. ✓ (A is singular)

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q4: verify A(adj A) = |A| I for A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = 11. Compute adj A (cofactors) and multiply: every diagonal entry is 11 and every off-diagonal entry 0, i.e. 11 I. ✓

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q5: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = 6 + 8 = 14. A⁻¹ =\[(1/14) \begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 \\ -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]=\[(1/14) \begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 \\ -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q6: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 5 \\ -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = −2 + 15 = 13. A⁻¹ =\[(1/13) \begin{bmatrix}2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q7: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = 1·2·5 = 10 (triangular). A⁻¹ =\[(1/10) \begin{bmatrix}10 & -10 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q8: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]
Ex 4.4 Q9: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 & 0 \\ -7 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Ex 4.4 Q10: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Ex 4.4 Q11: inverse of\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \cos  \alpha & \sin  \alpha \\ 0 & \sin  \alpha & -\cos  \alpha\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = −cos²α − sin²α = −1. The matrix equals its own inverse: A⁻¹ = A (A² = I)

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q12: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 7 \\ 2 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]B =\[\begin{bmatrix}6 & 8 \\ 7 & 9\end{bmatrix}\]Verify (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.
cards.definition: AB =\[\begin{bmatrix}67 & 87 \\ 47 & 61\end{bmatrix}\]|AB| = 4087 − 4089 = −2, so (AB)⁻¹ = −½\[\begin{bmatrix}61 & -87 \\ -47 & 67\end{bmatrix}\]Also A⁻¹ =\[\begin{bmatrix}5 & -7 \\ -2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]and B⁻¹ = −½\[\begin{bmatrix}9 & -8 \\ -7 & 6\end{bmatrix}\]the product B⁻¹A⁻¹ gives the same matrix. ✓

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q13: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]Show A² − 5A + 7I = O and find A⁻¹.
cards.definition: A² =\[\begin{bmatrix}8 & 5 \\ -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]From A² − 5A + 7I = O: A − 5I + 7A⁻¹ = O so A⁻¹ = (1/7)(5I − A) =\[(1/7) \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q14: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]Find a, b with A² + aA + bI = O.
cards.definition: For 2 × 2: A² − (tr A)A + (det A)I = O with tr A = 4, det A = 1. So a = −4, b = 1

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q15: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]Show A³ − 6A² + 5A + 11I = O and find A⁻¹.
cards.definition: Multiply by A⁻¹: A² − 6A + 5I + 11A⁻¹ = O, so A⁻¹ = −(1/11)(A² − 6A + 5I). A⁻¹ =\[(1/11) \begin{bmatrix}-3 & 4 & 5 \\ 9 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & -3 & -1\end{bmatrix}\](|A| = −11)

cards.term: Ex 4.4 Q16: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]Verify A³ − 6A² + 9A − 4I = O and find A⁻¹.
cards.definition: Multiply by A⁻¹: A² − 6A + 9I = 4A⁻¹. A⁻¹ =\[(1/4) \begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\](|A| = 4)

cards.term: Method: find A⁻¹ from a matrix equation like A² − 4A + I = O.
cards.definition: Multiply the whole equation by A⁻¹ (allowed since |A| ≠ 0), simplify A·A⁻¹ = I, and isolate A⁻¹. This is how Example 15 and Ex 4.4 Q13, Q15, Q16 work

cards.term: Cayley–Hamilton for a 2 × 2 matrix: what equation does A satisfy?
cards.definition: A² − (tr A) A + (det A) I = O. Example: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]: tr 4, det 1, so A² − 4A + I = O ✓

cards.term: What is a consistent / inconsistent system?
cards.definition: Consistent: at least one solution exists. Inconsistent: no solution

cards.term: Consistency test: |A| and (adj A)B
cards.definition: AX=B: |A|!=0 unique solution X = A^-1 B; |A|=0 and (adj A)B != O inconsistent (no solution); |A|=0 and (adj A)B = O: infinitely many solutions or none (check); lines intersect / parallel / coincide

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Consistency of linear systems

Match the tests “|A| ≠ 0”, “|A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O”, “|A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O” with these three pairs of lines.

Unique, none, or infinitely many?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Consistency of linear systems

Match the tests “|A| ≠ 0”, “|A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O”, “|A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O” with these three pairs of lines.

(a) x + 2y = 2 and 2x + 3y = 3 meet at one point: consistent, unique (|A| = −1 ≠ 0). (b) x + 3y = 5 and 2x + 6y = 8 are parallel: inconsistent (Ex 4.5 Q3). (c) The same line twice: consistent with infinitely many solutions.

In 3 variables the same test works: |A| ≠ 0 ⇒ unique solution X = A⁻¹B; |A| = 0 ⇒ compute (adj A)B.

cards.term: Matrix method for AX = B when |A| ≠ 0?
cards.definition: X = A⁻¹ B (unique solution). Set A = coefficients, X = unknowns, B = constants

cards.term: When |A| = 0 for AX = B, what do you check?
cards.definition: Compute (adj A)B. If it is ≠ O: inconsistent. If it is = O: the system has either infinitely many solutions or none

cards.term: Cramer’s rule (beyond the textbook, used in JEE): xᵢ = ?
cards.definition: xᵢ = Δᵢ/Δ, where Δ = |A| ≠ 0 and Δᵢ replaces the i-th column of A by B. Faster than the inverse for one unknown

cards.term: Homogeneous system AX = O: when does it have a non-trivial solution?
cards.definition: Iff |A| = 0. If |A| ≠ 0 the only solution is x = y = z = 0. (JEE: “find λ so the system has non-trivial solutions” ⇒ set the determinant to 0)

cards.term: Example 16: solve 2x + 5y = 1, 3x + 2y = 7.
Example 17: solve 3x − 2y + 3z = 8, 2x + y − z = 1, 4x − 3y + 2z = 4.
cards.definition: |A| = −17. Cofactors and A⁻¹ = (−1/17) adj A give x = 1, y = 2, z = 3

cards.term: Example 18: the sum of three numbers is 6; three times the third plus the second is 11; the first plus the third is double the second. Find them.
cards.definition: x + y + z = 6, y + 3z = 11, x − 2y + z = 0. |A| = 9, and X = A⁻¹B gives 1, 2, 3

cards.term: Example 19: use the product\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & -3 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]to solve x − y + 2z = 1, 2y − 3z = 1, 3x − 2y + 4z = 2.
cards.definition: The product is I, so the second matrix is A⁻¹. X = A⁻¹B = [−2 + 0 + 2, 9 + 2 − 6, 6 + 1 − 4]ᵀ: x = 0, y = 5, z = 3

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q1: is x + 2y = 2, 2x + 3y = 3 consistent?
cards.definition: |A| = 3 − 4 = −1 ≠ 0: consistent (unique solution x = 0, y = 1)

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q2: is 2x − y = 5, x + y = 4 consistent?
cards.definition: |A| = 2 + 1 = 3 ≠ 0: consistent

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q3: is x + 3y = 5, 2x + 6y = 8 consistent?
cards.definition: |A| = 6 − 6 = 0; adj A =\[\begin{bmatrix}6 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\](adj A)B = [30 − 24, −10 + 8]ᵀ = [6, −2]ᵀ ≠ O: inconsistent (parallel lines)

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q4: is x + y + z = 1, 2x + 3y + 2z = 2, ax + ay + 2az = 4 consistent?
cards.definition: |A| = 1(6a − 2a) − 1(4a − 2a) + 1(2a − 3a) = 4a − 2a − a = a ≠ 0, so consistent with a unique solution (for a ≠ 0)

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q5: is 3x − y − 2z = 2, 2y − z = −1, 3x − 5y = 3 consistent?
cards.definition: |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O: inconsistent

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q6: is 5x − y + 4z = 5, 2x + 3y + 5z = 2, 5x − 2y + 6z = −1 consistent?
Ex 4.5 Q7: solve 5x + 2y = 4, 7x + 3y = 5.
cards.definition: |A| = 1: x = 2, y = −3

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q8: solve 2x − y = −2, 3x + 4y = 3.
cards.definition: |A| = 11: x = −5/11, y = 12/11

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q9: solve 4x − 3y = 3, 3x − 5y = 7.
Ex 4.5 Q10: solve 5x + 2y = 3, 3x + 2y = 5.
cards.definition: Subtract: 2x = −2: x = −1, y = 4
|A| = 2(10 + 3) − 1(−5 − 0) + 1(3 − 0) = 34 ≠ 0. Matrix method gives x = 1, y = 1/2, z = −3/2 (check: 2 + ½ − 3/2 = 1 ✓)

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q12: solve x − y + z = 4, 2x + y − 3z = 0, x + y + z = 2.
cards.definition: x = 2, y = −1, z = 1
x = 1, y = 2, z = −1
x = 2, y = 1, z = 3

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q15: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]Find A⁻¹ and solve 2x − 3y + 5z = 11, 3x + 2y − 4z = −5, x + y − 2z = −3.
cards.definition: A⁻¹ =\[\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 9 & -23 \\ -1 & 5 & -13\end{bmatrix}\]Then X = A⁻¹[11, −5, −3]ᵀ gives x = 1, y = 2, z = 3

cards.term: Ex 4.5 Q16: 4 kg onion + 3 kg wheat + 2 kg rice = ₹60; 2 + 4 + 6 = ₹90; 6 + 2 + 3 = ₹70. Find the price per kg.
cards.definition: Solve 4x + 3y + 2z = 60, 2x + 4y + 6z = 90, 6x + 2y + 3z = 70: onion ₹5, wheat ₹8, rice ₹8

cards.term: Misc Q1: prove |x sin θ cos θ; −sin θ −x 1; cos θ 1 x| is independent of θ.
cards.definition: Expanding: x(−x² − 1) − sin θ(−x sin θ − cos θ) + cos θ(−sin θ + x cos θ) = −x³ − x + x sin²θ + sin θ cos θ − sin θ cos θ + x cos²θ = −x³ − x + x = −x³, free of θ

cards.term: Misc Q2: evaluate |cos α cos β, cos α sin β, −sin α; −sin β, cos β, 0; sin α cos β, sin α sin β, cos α|.
cards.definition: Expand along the second row (it has a zero): the two surviving terms combine to sin²β + cos²β = 1

cards.term: Misc Q3: A⁻¹ =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 & 1 \\ -15 & 6 & -5 \\ 5 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]and B =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]Find (AB)⁻¹.
cards.definition: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹. B⁻¹ =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]Multiplying:\[\begin{bmatrix}9 & -3 & 5 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term:
Misc Q4: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]Verify
(i) [adj A]⁻¹ = adj(A⁻¹)
(ii) (A⁻¹)⁻¹ = A.
cards.definition: Here |A| = −5. Since adj A = |A| A⁻¹, we get [adj A]⁻¹ = A/|A|, and adj(A⁻¹) = |A⁻¹| (A⁻¹)⁻¹ = A/|A|: equal. (ii) is the fact that inverting twice returns A. ✓

cards.term: Misc Q5: evaluate |x y x+y; y x+y x; x+y x y|.
cards.definition: Add all columns into column 1: (2x + 2y) times a column of 1s, factor it out, then reduce: −2(x³ + y³)

cards.term: Misc Q6: evaluate |1 x y; 1 x+y y; 1 x x+y|.
cards.definition: R₂ − R₁ and R₃ − R₁: |1 x y; 0 y 0; 0 0 x| = 1 · y · x = xy

cards.term:
Misc Q8: the inverse of diag(x, y, z) (non-zero x, y, z) is
(A) diag(1/x, 1/y, 1/z)
(B) xyz · diag(1/x, 1/y, 1/z)
(C) (1/xyz) diag(x, y, z)
(D) (1/xyz) I
cards.definition: Invert each diagonal entry: (A)

cards.term:
Misc Q9: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & \sin  \theta & 1 \\ -\sin  \theta & 1 & \sin  \theta \\ -1 & -\sin  \theta & 1\end{bmatrix}\]0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. Then Det A ∈
(A) {0}
(B) (2, ∞)
(C) (2, 4)
(D) [2, 4]
cards.definition: |A| = 2 + 2 sin²θ. With sin²θ ∈ [0, 1] this covers (D) [2, 4]

cards.term: Effect of transposing: |Aᵀ| = ?
cards.definition: |Aᵀ| = |A|. So anything true for rows is true for columns

cards.term: What happens to |A| if two rows (or columns) are interchanged?
cards.definition: It changes sign. So an even number of swaps leaves it unchanged

cards.term: What if two rows (or columns) are identical or proportional?
cards.definition: |A| = 0 (swapping the equal rows must change the sign but does not change the matrix, so |A| = −|A|)

cards.term: What if a row is multiplied by k?
cards.definition: |A| is multiplied by k. So a common factor of a row can be taken outside; for the whole matrix |kA| = kⁿ|A|

cards.term: Which row operation does not change the determinant?
cards.definition: Rᵢ → Rᵢ + kRⱼ (add a multiple of another row); same for columns. Use it to create zeros before expanding

cards.term: If every element of a row is a sum of two terms, what can you do?
cards.definition: Split into a sum of two determinants (the other rows unchanged): |a+p, b+q; c, d| = |a b; c d| + |p q; c d|

cards.term: Trap: is |A + B| = |A| + |B|?
cards.definition: No. The determinant is not additive. It is multiplicative: |AB| = |A||B|. Only the “one row is a sum” splitting works

cards.term: How do row operations help evaluate a determinant quickly? Example: |1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9|.
cards.definition: R₂ − R₁ = (3, 3, 3) and R₃ − R₂ = (3, 3, 3): two equal rows, so 0

cards.term: Determinant of a skew-symmetric matrix of odd order?
cards.definition: 0. |A| = |Aᵀ| = |−A| = (−1)ⁿ|A| = −|A| for odd n

cards.term: If A is n × n with A² = I, what are the possible values of |A|?
cards.definition: |A|² = 1 so |A| = ±1. Same if AAᵀ = I (orthogonal)

cards.term: If A is 3 × 3 with |A| = 2, find |3A|, |adj A|, |A⁻¹|, |A²|, |Aᵀ|.
cards.definition: |3A| = 27 · 2 = 54; |adj A| = |A|² = 4; |A⁻¹| = 1/2; |A²| = 4; |Aᵀ| = 2

cards.term: If A is 3 × 3, |A| = 4, find |adj(adj A)|.
cards.definition: |adj A| = |A|² = 16 and |adj(adj A)| = 16² = 256 = |A|⁴ (general: |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n−1)²))

cards.term: Vandermonde determinant |1 a a²; 1 b b²; 1 c c²| = ?
cards.definition: (b − a)(c − a)(c − b). It vanishes iff two of a, b, c are equal. Ex 4.3 Q4 is the similar (x − y)(y − z)(z − x)

cards.term: Circulant/symmetric trick: |a b c; b c a; c a b| = ?
cards.definition: −(a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) = −(a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

cards.term: Determinant of a triangular 4 × 4 matrix with diagonal 1, 2, 3, 4?
cards.definition: Product of the diagonal entries: 24

cards.term: For which k is\[\begin{bmatrix}k & 2 \\ 3 & k + 1\end{bmatrix}\]singular?
cards.definition: k(k + 1) − 6 = 0 → k² + k − 6 = 0 → k = 2 or −3
(x + 1)(x + 3) − 15 = x² + 4x − 12 = 0 → x = 2 or x = −6

cards.term: For which λ does x + y + z = 0, x + 2y + 3z = 0, 2x + 3y + λz = 0 have non-trivial solutions?
cards.definition: Determinant |1 1 1; 1 2 3; 2 3 λ| = (2λ − 9) − (λ − 6) + (3 − 4) = λ − 4 = 0 → λ = 4

cards.term: Area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (a, 0), (0, b) using the determinant?
cards.definition: ½ |0 0 1; a 0 1; 0 b 1| = ½ · |ab| = ab/2
10 + 12 = (b) 22

cards.term:
MCQ: if A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 5, then |2A| =
(a) 10 (b) 40 (c) 25 (d) 125
cards.definition: 2³ · 5 = (b) 40

cards.term:
MCQ: if A is a square matrix of order 3 with |A| = −4, then |adj A| =
(a) −4 (b) 4 (c) 16 (d) −16
cards.definition: |A|² = (c) 16

cards.term:
MCQ: the value of |1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9| is
(a) 0 (b) 1 (c) −1 (d) 3
cards.definition: (a) 0 (rows in arithmetic progression)

cards.term:
MCQ: the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3) is
(a) 12 (b) 6 (c) 3 (d) 7
cards.definition: ½ · 4 · 3 = (b) 6

cards.term:
MCQ: for what value of k are the points (k, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6) collinear?
(a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 3 (d) 4
cards.definition: Slope between the last two is 1, so (k, 2) lies on y = x + 1: k = 1: (a) 1

cards.term:
MCQ: if A is invertible and |A| = 3, then |A⁻¹| =
(a) 3 (b) 1/3 (c) −3 (d) 9
cards.definition: (b) 1/3

cards.term:
MCQ: if A =\[\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]then A⁻¹ =
(a)\[(1/5) \begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix} (b) \begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\](c)\[(1/5) \begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}\](d)\[(1/5) \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
cards.definition: |A| = 5: (a)

cards.term:
MCQ: the system x + y = 2, 2x + 2y = 5 is
(a) consistent, unique (b) inconsistent (c) consistent, infinitely many (d) none
cards.definition: |A| = 0 and the equations are parallel: (b) inconsistent

cards.term:
MCQ: if the system 2x + 3y = 5, kx + 6y = 10 has infinitely many solutions, k =
(a) 4 (b) 6 (c) 2 (d) 3
cards.definition: The second is twice the first: (a) 4

cards.term: Integer answer (JEE Main): if A is 3 × 3 with |A| = 2, the value of |adj(2A)| is?
cards.definition: |2A| = 8·2 = 16, |adj(2A)| = 16² = 256

cards.term: Integer answer: the number of values of k for which\[\begin{bmatrix}k & 1 \\ 1 & k\end{bmatrix}\]is singular is?
cards.definition: k² − 1 = 0 gives k = ±1: 2

cards.term: Integer answer: if |x 2; 3 4| = 10, the value of x is?
cards.definition: 4x − 6 = 10, so x = 4

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: |A| = 0 implies A has no inverse.
R: A⁻¹ = adj A / |A| requires division by |A|.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: |A + B| = |A| + |B|.
R: |AB| = |A||B|.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A false, R true (d) Both false
cards.definition: (c): R is true; A is false in general

cards.term: True/False: interchanging two rows of a determinant does not change its value.
cards.definition: False: the sign changes

cards.term: True/False: |A| ≠ 0 means the system AX = B has a unique solution.
cards.definition: True: X = A⁻¹B

cards.term: 2-mark: find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 1), (3, 5), (−2, 4).
3-mark: find the adjoint of A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]and verify A(adj A) = |A| I.
cards.definition: adj A =\[\begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]|A| = −2. A(adj A) =\[\begin{bmatrix}4 - 6 & -2 + 2 \\ 12 - 12 & -6 + 4\end{bmatrix}\]= −2 I ✓

cards.term: 3-mark: solve x + y = 3, 2x − y = 0 by the matrix method.
cards.definition: A =\[\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]|A| = −3, A⁻¹ =\[(-1/3) \begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]X = A⁻¹[3, 0]ᵀ = [1, 2]ᵀ: x = 1, y = 2

cards.term: 4-mark: solve x − y + z = 4, 2x + y − 3z = 0, x + y + z = 2 by the matrix method.
cards.definition: |A| = 1(1 + 3) + 1(2 + 3) + 1(2 − 1) = 10. Solving via A⁻¹B: x = 2, y = −1, z = 1

cards.term: 4-mark: if A =\[\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]show A² − 5A + 7I = O and hence find A⁻¹.
cards.definition: A² =\[\begin{bmatrix}8 & 5 \\ -5 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]A² − 5A + 7I = O. Multiply by A⁻¹: A − 5I + 7A⁻¹ = O, so A⁻¹ = (1/7)(5I − A) =\[(1/7) \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]

cards.term: Case-based: 2 pens + 3 pencils + 1 eraser cost ₹19; 1 pen + 2 pencils + 2 erasers cost ₹14; 3 pens + 1 pencil + 1 eraser cost ₹17. Find the prices.
cards.definition: Solve 2x + 3y + z = 19, x + 2y + 2z = 14, 3x + y + z = 17. |A| = 10 ≠ 0 and the matrix method gives pen ₹4, pencil ₹3, eraser ₹2 (check: 8 + 9 + 2 = 19 ✓)
